text: Security and governance questions on DP-700 read like a scenario, and the four options are almost always four real Fabric controls — just at different layers. Only one of them is the right layer for that scenario.

Workspace role controls every item in a workspace. Item permission narrows that to one item. A OneLake data access role narrows it further to specific folders and tables. Row-level security narrows it again to specific rows, inside a semantic model.
OneLake data access roles scope access inside one lakehouse. Sensitivity labels attach to the data itself and travel with exports. Row-level security lives in the semantic model, not the lakehouse.
A sensitivity label on a warehouse table doesn't reset when a report is exported — it persists, because it's Purview-backed and rides with the data, not the workspace.
The pattern: pick the narrowest control that satisfies the scenario, not the broadest one that would also work. Next up: the same pattern applied to monitoring and deployment.
